result.title: Interpretable Meta-Policies for Neural Decision Making
result.summary: Deep Reinforcement Learning remains difficult to interpret and align due to the black-box nature of neural networks. While (neuro-)symbolic approaches improve transparency by incorporating symbolic reasoning, applying them directly to low-level actions results in overly complex, unreadable policies. We introduce NEXUS, a hierarchical RL framework that resolves this tension by combining neural skills with symbolic meta-policies. By shifting transparent reasoning to high-level skills rather than atomic actions, NEXUS drastically reduces symbolic complexity without sacrificing environment performance. Object-centric observations enable high-level reasoning and the design of reward functions and meta-policies by interaction with LLMs. We demonstrate that NEXUS agents learn disentangled skills, are interpretable regarding high-level goals, are better aligned to goals described in the game manual, less prone to reward hacking and more robust to game simplifications than deep RL. Finally, we isolate and evaluate the impact of different meta-policy architectures (neural, symbolic, neuro-symbolic) on environmental return and aligned task performance.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 NEXUS 分层强化学习框架，将神经技能与符号元策略结合，把透明推理放在高层技能而非原子动作上，借助对象中心观测与 LLM 设计奖励和元策略，并比较神经、符号、神经符号三类元策略架构。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「高层符号选择 + 低层神经技能」的状态抽象与决策分层，可能为 LVR 中在哪里施加可解释的高层选择与停止决策提供参照；但该文不涉及视觉语言推理与 latent 证据使用，需较多核查。
